newsitem.title: GERMANY: Swedish minister says Sweden can qualify for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Swedish minister says Sweden can qualify for EMU.

text.p: Swedish Industry and Commerce Minister Leif Pagrotsky said on Tuesday Sweden would definitely qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU) if it decided it wanted to join.

"We will definitely be in a position to join if we decide to join," Pagrotsky told a news conference after talks with German Economy Minister Guenter Rexrodt. "But we will have to wait another six months before we can tell more accurately."
Pagrotsky said there was a broad public discussion on the issue in Sweden. "Public opinion is rather sceptical so far, but also rather volatile," he said.

Pagrotsky said he had raised his worries about rising unemployment in Europe, which could turn public opinion against the idea of EMU, with Rexrodt. But he said he still thought EMU would go ahead on schedule in 1999.

"I expressed my worries for rising unemployment in Europe and the co-ordinated fiscal tightening taking place all across Europe which could give rise to public discontentment and render monetary union more difficult," he said.
"I don't see any need for tighter economic policies in western Europe. There's no inflation danger now," he said.
